info.name: E-Library API — Milestone 3 — Complete Automated QA
info.description: Milestone 3 automated file-management QA. The collection references generated local files under postman/m3-test-files/. Run Newman from the project root so relative file paths resolve. Postman Desktop may require the collection's working directory/local file access permission. Setup automatically selects the first available book as m3ReferenceBookId. Error assertions follow the project's current error response contract. For Newman, run from this package directory (or pass --working-dir to this directory); file sources are relative to m3-postman-package/.

request.description: Regression test for the uploaded errorHandler. Current code converts MulterError to ApiError(500) before reaching its MulterError branch, so this is expected to expose the bug until the handler is fixed.
Known QA finding: service uploads to Cloudinary before Book.findById(), so this can return 404 while leaving an orphan Cloudinary asset. Verify manually in Cloudinary.

request.description: Manual DB check after operations. Cover upload: coverImage.url/publicId/format/sizeBytes/originalName/uploadedAt populated. Replace: publicId changes. Delete: target object is exactly {}. PDF/EPUB operations populate only their own nested key; uploading PDF must not alter EPUB metadata and vice versa.

Manual Cloudinary check. Correct folders: e-library/covers/, e-library/pdfs/, e-library/epubs/. publicId format: book-<bookId>-<type>-<timestamp>. Compare Cloudinary size with MongoDB sizeBytes. Old asset must disappear after replace; deleted asset must no longer exist.

item.name: M3-CLOUD-002 Known orphan risk — nonexistent book

request.description: After TC-M3-012, search Cloudinary for the fake-book publicId. QA guide identifies a confirmed ordering bug: uploadBuffer() occurs before Book.findById(), so a 404 can leave an orphan Cloudinary asset.

Current uploaded errorHandler returns errors as { success:false, message, optional details, optional stack in development }. It does NOT include statusCode in the JSON error body. ApiResponse includes statusCode only on successful responses. Postman error tests therefore assert HTTP status + success:false + message, not json.statusCode.
